items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: Bill Haley. Bill Haley. Bill Haley. Bill Haley, who got to rock tonight.

ctx.x: Well, when you hear that terminology, what does that mean? You heard it in the mid-fifties. You first heard it.

Well, when I first heard it, I looked at it and said, rock and roll. Well, you see, Roy Brown, like I said, really started this thing in New Orleans, even before Fats Domino, in a sense, because he had this good rock and tonight thing, and he had this band with Bob Bob Ockton. Bob Ockton was an ordinary, but he was a drummer. He died a couple of years back, you know, and incidentally, some of his relatives say, no, I'm no real business right now. I talk to him every now and then. So, when you're good rocking…

Well, well, did you, I know you probably did, and there's a whole article in the Jazz Archivist. Yeah. And we're talking about New Orleans in the 60s, and they're talking about, a lot of it about the modern jazz scene. Did you follow the pop, the bebop scene in New Orleans?
